claims.text: Equimolar WTaTiVZr has greater high-temperature plastic strain than commercially pure tungsten.
Equimolar WTaTiVZr has greater high-temperature toughness than commercially pure tungsten.
Severe lattice distortion in WTaTiVZr produces fine-scale dual-phase structures or heterogeneous grain boundaries.
Fine-scale interfaces in WTaTiVZr promote dislocation absorption.
Fine-scale interfaces in WTaTiVZr promote localized grain-boundary sliding.
Fine-scale interfaces in WTaTiVZr deflect propagating cracks.
As-synthesized equimolar WTaTiVZr is a homogeneous, lattice-distorted solid solution.
As-synthesized equimolar WTaTiVZr contains incipient nanoscale phase boundaries.
Commercially pure tungsten has a relatively uniform microstructure.
Distorted and heterogeneous boundaries in WTaTiVZr act as effective dislocation sinks.
At high temperature, boundary-mediated processes redistribute and dissipate stress in WTaTiVZr.
Boundary-mediated processes promote dislocation movement in WTaTiVZr at high temperature.
Stress redistribution, dislocation motion, grain-boundary sliding, and crack deflection increase the plastic strain and toughness of WTaTiVZr.
WTaTiVZr will exhibit significantly greater tensile elongation than pure tungsten at 800–1200 °C under the proposed service-relevant atmosphere.
WTaTiVZr will exhibit significantly greater fracture toughness or energy absorption before failure than pure tungsten at 800–1200 °C.
Pure tungsten typically has limited plastic strain and lower toughness under comparable high-temperature conditions because its uniform microstructure is less accommodating.
The proposed mechanism operates predominantly at temperatures where dislocation mobility and grain-boundary sliding are active.
The effect of the proposed mechanism may be minimal at lower temperatures.

contradictions.description: The initial alloy is described as a homogeneous solid solution, while the governing microstructure is described as fine-scale dual-phase. Incipient phase boundaries could potentially reconcile these descriptions, but no phase evolution during testing is specified.
